catalyst_text: Announced positive phase 1 results in healthy volunteers
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive phase 1 data in healthy volunteers showed deep and sustained IgG reduction with a favorable safety profile. The study also demonstrated an extended half-life of 15–18 days, supporting a differentiated pharmacologic profile.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viridian Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:VRDN), a biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing potential best-in-class medicines for autoimmune and rare diseases, today announced positive phase 1 results for VRDN-008. The phase 1 clinical trial evaluated subcutaneous VRDN-008 in healthy volunteers. VRDN-008 demonstrated deep and sustained IgG reduction through 8 weeks after dosing in healthy volunteers, with 74% IgG reduction at peak. Confirmed half-life extension: VRDN-008 demonstrated an extended half-life of 15–18 days, up to 6x longer than the first-generation Fc fragments. VRDN-008 demonstrated a safety profile that spared albumin and LDL and was generally well-tolerated, with no serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities in the trial.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for thyroid eye disease
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) to treat thyroid eye disease, with labeling inclusive of active and chronic disease. The decision was supported by two Phase 3 trials meeting primary and secondary endpoints and marks the first commercial product for this program.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viridian Therapeutics (NASDAQ:VRDN) announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Lumvoa™ (veligrotug-vvze) for the treatment of thyroid eye disease, marking the company's first commercial product. According to the company, Lumvoa is the first approved therapy for thyroid eye disease with labeling that includes data for both active and chronic disease. The approval was supported by two Phase 3 clinical trials that met their primary and secondary endpoints.

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for thyroid eye disease
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved Lumvoa for the treatment of thyroid eye disease, including both active and chronic forms. Approval was supported by the pivotal THRIVE and THRIVE-2 phase 3 trials, which met all primary and secondary endpoints with clinically meaningful improvements.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viridian Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:VRDN), a biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing potentially best-in-class medicines for autoimmune and rare diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Lumvoa™ (veligrotug-vvze) for the treatment of thyroid eye disease (TED). Lumvoa was approved by the FDA under Priority Review and supported by the THRIVE (active TED) and THRIVE-2 (chronic TED) pivotal phase 3 clinical trials. Both the THRIVE and THRIVE-2 clinical trials met their respective primary and all secondary endpoints, consistently demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements at week 15 across all of the key signs and symptoms of TED. Lumvoa is a full antagonist of IGF-1R and the first approved treatment for TED with labeling that includes data for both active and chronic TED.

catalyst_text: BLA accepted with priority review and PDUFA date
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA accepted the BLA and granted Priority Review, assigning a PDUFA target action date of 2026-06-30. This establishes the regulatory timeline for the program in thyroid eye disease. Priority Review indicates an expedited review based on potential benefit.
catalyst_text_evidence: Veligrotug was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the FDA, and its BLA is under Priority Review at the FDA with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of June 30, 2026.

catalyst_text: Trial met primary endpoint with highly significant results
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported positive topline results from the Phase 3 REVEAL-2 study in chronic thyroid eye disease, meeting FDA and EMA primary endpoints with high statistical significance. Proptosis responder rates were 50% and 54% for Q4W and Q8W dosing versus 15% for placebo, and diplopia response was significant in the Q4W arm. These results add pivotal evidence supporting a potential subcutaneous treatment option.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viridian Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:VRDN)... today announced positive topline data from the REVEAL‑2 phase 3 clinical trial of elegrobart in patients with chronic thyroid eye disease (TED). REVEAL-2 met its primary endpoint for both the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and European Medicines Agency (EMA) with high statistical significance (p < 0.0001). Elegrobart Q4W and Q8W achieved 50% and 54% proptosis responder rates (PRR) at week 24, respectively, versus 15% placebo, both highly statistically significant results (p < 0.0001).

catalyst_text: Announced positive phase 3 topline results in TED
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from the REVEAL-1 phase 3 trial in active thyroid eye disease were reported, meeting the primary endpoint of proptosis responder rate with high statistical significance. Additional endpoints, including proptosis mean change and diplopia measures, showed clinically meaningful improvements. These data support a convenient subcutaneous autoinjector approach and advance the program toward regulatory submission.
catalyst_text_evidence: Viridian Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:VRDN), a biotechnology company focused on discovering, developing, and commercializing potentially best-in-class medicines for serious and rare diseases, 2026-03-30 announced positive topline data from the elegrobart REVEAL-1 phase 3 clinical trial in patients with active thyroid eye disease (TED). REVEAL-1 met its primary endpoint with high statistical significance. REVEAL-1 was highly statistically significant on its primary endpoint of Q4W proptosis responder rate and the key secondary endpoint of Q4W proptosis mean change from baseline, each at week 24 as measured by exophthalmometry.

catalyst_text: BLA accepted priority review PDUFA June 30 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The biologics application is under FDA Priority Review with a target action date of 2026-06-30 for thyroid eye disease. Acceptance and priority review establish a definitive review timeline and indicate an expedited evaluation. This milestone guides expectations for potential approval and commercialization planning.
catalyst_text_evidence: The veligrotug BLA is under Priority Review at the FDA with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of 2026-06-30. Veligrotug also received both Breakthrough Therapy Designation and Priority Review from the FDA in 2025.

catalyst_text: Reported positive long-term data from the Phase 3 THRIVE trial, with 70% of veligrotug-treated proptosis responders at week 15 maintaining their response through week 52 in patients with active Thyroid Eye Disease.
FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to veligrotug, the company’s lead anti-insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) drug candidate.
The data from Phase 3 shared during the Webcast met all primary and secondary endpoints, as reported on September 10, 2024.
The enrollment target for Phase 1/2 was surpassed because of high patient interest, with 188 patients signing up, around 40% of whom were from US locations, as reported on July 25, 2024.
